lessons.title: Walking vs going

sentences.target: Сейчас я иду домой.
sentences.english: Right now I'm walking home.
sentences.translit: Seychas ya idu domoy.

sentences.target: Я хожу на работу каждый день.
sentences.english: I walk to work every day.
sentences.translit: Ya khozhu na rabotu kazhdyy den'.

sentences.target: Мы едем на поезде в Москву.
sentences.english: We're going to Moscow by train.
sentences.translit: My yedem na poyezde v Moskvu.

sentences.target: Он часто ездит на машине.
sentences.english: He often goes by car.
sentences.translit: On chasto yezdit na mashine.

sentences.target: Она бежит, потому что опаздывает.
sentences.english: She's running because she's late.
sentences.translit: Ona bezhit, potomu shto opazdyvayet.

sentences.target: Я не люблю летать на самолёте.
sentences.english: I don't like flying by plane.
sentences.translit: Ya ne lyublyu letat' na samolyote.

fills.english: Right now I'm walking to the shop.
Every morning I go to the park.
Tomorrow we're going to Moscow by train.
In summer I like swimming in the sea.

dialogue.scene: Bumping into a friend on the street

lines.english: Hi! Where are you going?

lines.target: Я иду на работу. А ты?
lines.english: I'm walking to work. And you?
lines.translit: Ya idu na rabotu. A ty?

lines.target: Я тоже! Как ты обычно ездишь?
lines.english: Me too! How do you usually get there?
lines.translit: Ya tozhe! Kak ty obychno yezdish'?

replyOptions: Я езжу на метро каждый день.

lessons.tip: Paired verbs: идти/ехать = one trip happening now; ходить/ездить = habit or round trip. Same idea for every pair.

lessons.title: Prefixed motion

sentences.target: Мы приехали в город вечером.
sentences.english: We arrived in the city in the evening.
sentences.translit: My priyekhali v gorod vecherom.

sentences.target: Он уехал в понедельник и ещё не вернулся.
sentences.english: He left on Monday and hasn't come back yet.
sentences.translit: On uyekhal v ponedel'nik i yeshchyo ne vernulsya.

sentences.target: Я вышла из дома в восемь утра.
sentences.english: I left the house at eight in the morning.
sentences.translit: Ya vyshla iz doma v vosem' utra.

sentences.target: Зайди ко мне в гости после работы!
sentences.english: Drop by my place after work!
sentences.translit: Zaydi ko mne v gosti posle raboty!

sentences.target: Как мне дойти до вокзала?
sentences.english: How do I get to the station on foot?
sentences.translit: Kak mne doyti do vokzala?

sentences.target: Мы вернулись домой поздно ночью.
sentences.english: We got home late at night.
sentences.translit: My vernulis' domoy pozdno noch'yu.

fills.english: We arrived in Moscow yesterday evening.

fills.after: из дома и пошла в магазин.
fills.english: She went out of the house and walked to the shop.
Could you tell me how to get to the metro?
After work I dropped by the bakery.

dialogue.scene: Phoning a friend who is late

lines.target: Алло! Ты уже вышел из дома?
lines.english: Hello! Have you left the house yet?
lines.translit: Allo! Ty uzhe vyshel iz doma?

lines.english: Yes, I'm already on my way.
When will you get here?

replyOptions: Через двадцать минут, я уже близко.
Я иду туда и обратно каждый день.

lessons.tip: Prefix = direction: при- arrive, у- leave, вы- out, в- in, за- drop by. Prefix + идти/ехать gives a perfective verb.

lessons.title: Story connectors

items.english: once upon a time / one time

sentences.target: Однажды я потерял телефон в метро.
sentences.english: Once I lost my phone on the metro.
sentences.translit: Odnazhdy ya poteryal telefon v metro.

sentences.target: В тот день шёл сильный дождь.
sentences.english: That day it was raining hard.
sentences.translit: V tot den' shyol sil'nyy dozhd'.

sentences.target: Вдруг он замолчал и посмотрел на меня.
sentences.english: Suddenly he went quiet and looked at me.
sentences.translit: Vdrug on zamolchal i posmotrel na menya.

sentences.target: Тем временем мой брат ждал меня на вокзале.
sentences.english: Meanwhile my brother was waiting for me at the station.
sentences.translit: Tem vremenem moy brat zhdal menya na vokzale.

sentences.target: Оказалось, что магазин закрыт.
sentences.english: It turned out the shop was closed.
sentences.translit: Okazalos', shto magazin zakryt.

sentences.target: Короче, мы просто пошли домой.
sentences.english: Long story short, we just went home.
sentences.translit: Koroche, my prosto poshli domoy.

fills.after: я встретил старого друга в кафе.
fills.english: Once I met an old friend in a café.
I was sitting at home and suddenly the phone rang.
In the end we found a good flat.
It turned out he's my neighbour!

dialogue.scene: Telling a friend about your weekend

lines.english: So how was your weekend?
Imagine, I lost my keys!
Awful! And what happened next?

replyOptions: В конце концов я нашёл их в сумке.
Я люблю ключи, потому что они дорогие.

lessons.tip: Linking words do the heavy lifting: однажды sets the scene, вдруг makes the twist, в конце концов wraps it up.

lessons.title: Narrating

items.english: it worked out / it turned out

sentences.target: Я рассказал ему всю историю.
sentences.english: I told him the whole story.
sentences.translit: Ya rasskazal yemu vsyu istoriyu.

sentences.target: Что случилось? Ты такой грустный!
sentences.english: What happened? You look so sad!
sentences.translit: Shto sluchilos'? Ty takoy grustnyy!

sentences.target: Мы шли по улице и вдруг заметили собаку.
sentences.english: We were walking down the street and suddenly noticed a dog.
sentences.translit: My shli po ulitse i vdrug zametili sobaku.

sentences.target: Она испугалась и закричала.
sentences.english: She got scared and screamed.
sentences.translit: Ona ispugalas' i zakrichala.

sentences.target: Я так удивился, что замолчал.
sentences.english: I was so surprised that I fell silent.
sentences.translit: Ya tak udivilsya, shto zamolchal.

sentences.target: Мы смеялись всю ночь, а потом я заплакал.
sentences.english: We laughed all night, and then I started crying.
sentences.translit: My smeyalis' vsyu noch', a potom ya zaplakal.

fills.english: Yesterday I talked for ages about the trip.

fills.after: ключи на столе и взял их.
fills.english: I noticed the keys on the table and took them.
When I came in, everyone fell silent and looked at me.
What happened last night?

dialogue.scene: A friend looks upset

lines.english: I've been quiet all day.
Did something happen?

lines.target: Да. Я не знаю, что делать.
lines.english: Yes. I don't know what to do.
lines.translit: Da. Ya ne znayu, shto delat'.

lessons.tip: Imperfective past = scene or process (я читал = I was reading); perfective past = a finished event (я прочитал = I finished it).

lessons.title: Memories

sentences.target: В детстве я жил в маленьком городе.
sentences.english: In my childhood I lived in a small town.
sentences.translit: V detstve ya zhil v malen'kom gorode.

sentences.target: Раньше мы часто ходили в кино.
sentences.english: We used to go to the cinema often.
sentences.translit: Ran'she my chasto khodili v kino.

sentences.target: Когда я был маленьким, я любил футбол.
sentences.english: When I was little, I loved football.
sentences.translit: Kogda ya byl malen'kim, ya lyubil futbol.

sentences.target: В университете я много читал и мало спал.
sentences.english: At university I read a lot and slept little.
sentences.translit: V universitete ya mnogo chital i malo spal.

sentences.target: Я помню этот день, как будто это было вчера.
sentences.english: I remember that day as if it was yesterday.
sentences.translit: Ya pomnyu etot den', kak budto eto bylo vchera.

sentences.target: Мы жили там десять лет назад.
sentences.english: We lived there ten years ago.
sentences.translit: My zhili tam desyat' let nazad.

fills.english: I used to live in England, now I'm here.
I don't remember his name.
Three years ago we moved to a new house.

fills.after: я был в отпуске в Турции.
fills.english: Last year I was on holiday in Turkey.

dialogue.scene: Chatting about the past with an old friend

lines.english: Do you remember our old courtyard?

lines.target: Конечно помню! Мы там играли в футбол.
lines.english: Of course I do! We played football there.
lines.translit: Koneshno pomnyu! My tam igrali v futbol.

lines.english: And where did you live before?

replyOptions: Раньше я жил в маленьком городе.
Раньше я буду жить в Москве.

lessons.tip: Раньше + imperfective = used to. Раньше я жил в Москве = I used to live in Moscow.

lessons.title: Comparatives

sentences.target: Этот телефон лучше, но он дороже.
sentences.english: This phone is better, but it's more expensive.
sentences.translit: Etot telefon luchshe, no on dorozhe.

sentences.target: Автобус медленнее, чем метро.
sentences.english: The bus is slower than the metro.
sentences.translit: Avtobus medlenneye, chem metro.

sentences.target: Мой дом ближе к центру, чем твой.
sentences.english: My house is closer to the centre than yours.
sentences.translit: Moy dom blizhe k tsentru, chem tvoy.

sentences.target: Сегодня погода хуже, чем вчера.
sentences.english: The weather is worse today than yesterday.
sentences.translit: Sevodnya pogoda khuzhe, chem vchera.

sentences.target: Можно дешевле? Это слишком дорого.
sentences.english: Can it be cheaper? That's too expensive.
sentences.translit: Mozhno deshevle? Eto slishkom dorogo.

sentences.target: Мне нужно больше времени и меньше работы.
sentences.english: I need more time and less work.
sentences.translit: Mne nuzhno bol'she vremeni i men'she raboty.

fills.english: The train is faster than the bus.
This shop is cheaper than that one.
The station is farther than the park.
I feel better today, thanks.

dialogue.scene: Choosing a flat with an agent

lines.target: Вот две квартиры. Первая дороже, но ближе к метро.
lines.english: Here are two flats. The first is more expensive but closer to the metro.
lines.translit: Vot dve kvartiry. Pervaya dorozhe, no blizhe k metro.

lines.english: And the second one?

lines.target: Она дешевле и больше, но дальше от центра.
lines.english: It's cheaper and bigger, but farther from the centre.
lines.translit: Ona deshevle i bol'she, no dal'she ot tsentra.

replyOptions: Вторая лучше, мне нужно больше места.
Первая дальше, потому что она ближе.

lessons.tip: Comparatives never change for gender or case: быстрее, дороже, больше. Learn them as single words.

lessons.title: Comparing

sentences.target: Я работаю больше, чем он.
sentences.english: I work more than he does.
sentences.translit: Ya rabotayu bol'she, chem on.

sentences.target: У меня такой же телефон, как у тебя.
sentences.english: I have the same phone as you.
sentences.translit: U menya takoy zhe telefon, kak u tebya.

sentences.target: По сравнению с Москвой это маленький город.
sentences.english: Compared to Moscow it's a small city.
sentences.translit: Po sravneniyu s Moskvoy eto malen'kiy gorod.

sentences.target: Это самая красивая улица в нашем городе.
sentences.english: This is the most beautiful street in our city.
sentences.translit: Eto samaya krasivaya ulitsa v nashem gorode.

sentences.target: Это один из лучших фильмов года.
sentences.english: It's one of the best films of the year.
sentences.translit: Eto odin iz luchshikh fil'mov goda.

sentences.target: Он говорит гораздо быстрее, чем я.
sentences.english: He speaks much faster than I do.
sentences.translit: On govorit gorazdo bystreye, chem ya.

fills.english: My brother is three years older than me.
We have the same house as they do.
It's the biggest city in the country.
It's much cheaper here than in the centre.

dialogue.scene: Comparing two cafés

lines.english: Have you been to the new café?

lines.target: Да, там кофе лучше, чем здесь.
lines.english: Yes, the coffee's better there than here.
lines.translit: Da, tam kofe luchshe, chem zdes'.

lines.english: Really? And the prices?

replyOptions: По сравнению с вчера я хотел.

lessons.tip: Two ways to compare: быстрее, чем он (чем + nominative) or быстрее него (genitive, no чем).

lessons.title: Superlatives

sentences.target: Это самый лучший день в моей жизни.
sentences.english: This is the best day of my life.
sentences.translit: Eto samyy luchshiy den' v moyey zhizni.

sentences.target: Самый большой город в стране — это столица.
sentences.english: The biggest city in the country is the capital.
sentences.translit: Samyy bol'shoy gorod v strane — eto stolitsa.

sentences.target: Мы пошли в самый популярный ресторан.
sentences.english: We went to the most popular restaurant.
sentences.translit: My poshli v samyy populyarnyy restoran.

sentences.target: Это самая сложная работа, которую я делал.
sentences.english: This is the hardest job I've done.
sentences.translit: Eto samaya slozhnaya rabota, kotoruyu ya delal.

sentences.target: Самое важное — это семья.
sentences.english: The most important thing is family.
sentences.translit: Samoye vazhnoye — eto sem'ya.

sentences.target: Твой план самый простой, давай его сделаем.
sentences.english: Your plan is the simplest, let's do it.
sentences.translit: Tvoy plan samyy prostoy, davay yevo sdelayem.

fills.english: This is the most interesting film I've watched.
Mum makes the tastiest soup in the world.
This is the most beautiful square in the city.
They sell the most expensive watches here.

dialogue.scene: Choosing a restaurant for the evening

lines.english: Where shall we go for dinner?

lines.target: Есть один ресторан, там самое вкусное мясо.
lines.english: There's a restaurant with the tastiest meat.
lines.translit: Yest' odin restoran, tam samoye vkusnoye myaso.

lines.english: Is it expensive?

replyOptions: Не самый дорогой, но очень популярный.

lessons.tip: самый + adjective agrees with its noun: самый вкусный суп, самая вкусная еда, самое вкусное мясо, самые вкусные яблоки.

lessons.title: Describing objects

sentences.target: Это хорошее качество за такую цену.
sentences.english: That's good quality for such a price.
sentences.translit: Eto khorosheye kachestvo za takuyu tsenu.

sentences.target: Мне нравится этот стиль, он очень удобный.
sentences.english: I like this style, it's very comfortable.
sentences.translit: Mne nravitsya etot stil', on ochen' udobnyy.

sentences.target: Диван мягкий, а стул твёрдый.
sentences.english: The sofa is soft and the chair is hard.
sentences.translit: Divan myagkiy, a stul tvyordyy.

sentences.target: Какая это марка? Она дорогая?
sentences.english: What brand is that? Is it expensive?
sentences.translit: Kakaya eto marka? Ona dorogaya?

sentences.target: Сумка тяжёлая, потому что в ней много книг.
sentences.english: The bag is heavy because it has lots of books in it.
sentences.translit: Sumka tyazhyolaya, potomu shto v ney mnogo knig.

sentences.target: Из какого материала эта футболка?
sentences.english: What material is this T-shirt made of?
sentences.translit: Iz kakovo materiala eta futbolka?

fills.english: This sofa is very comfortable, I love it.
I have a heavy bag, help me!
The bed is soft and I sleep well.
The kitchen is always clean because Mum loves things tidy.

dialogue.scene: Buying a new armchair

lines.english: Do you like this armchair?
It's comfortable, but what's the material?
It's a durable material, good quality.

lessons.tip: Adjectives copy the noun: удобный стул (m), удобная кровать (f), удобное кресло (n), удобные стулья (pl).

lessons.title: Cities & countries

sentences.target: Столица больше, чем наш город.
sentences.english: The capital is bigger than our city.
sentences.translit: Stolitsa bol'she, chem nash gorod.

sentences.target: Население города — два миллиона человек.
sentences.english: The city's population is two million people.
sentences.translit: Naseleniye goroda — dva milliona chelovek.

sentences.target: Расстояние до центра — десять километров.
sentences.english: The distance to the centre is ten kilometres.
sentences.translit: Rasstoyaniye do tsentra — desyat' kilometrov.

sentences.target: Я живу в пригороде, там тише, чем в центре.
sentences.english: I live in a suburb, it's quieter than in the centre.
sentences.translit: Ya zhivu v prigorode, tam tishe, chem v tsentre.

sentences.target: Зарплата здесь выше, но налоги тоже выше.
sentences.english: Salaries are higher here, but taxes are also higher.
sentences.translit: Zarplata zdes' vyshe, no nalogi tozhe vyshe.

sentences.target: По сравнению с Москвой здесь безопаснее.
sentences.english: Compared to Moscow it's safer here.
sentences.translit: Po sravneniyu s Moskvoy zdes' bezopasneye.

fills.english: In the centre there's noise, and in the suburb it's quiet.
My district is cleaner than yours.
Salaries in the capital are higher than in the region.
Compared to the village, the city is very noisy.

dialogue.scene: Thinking about moving abroad

lines.english: Do you want to move to the capital?

lines.target: Да, там зарплата выше, чем у нас.
lines.english: Yes, salaries are higher there than here.
lines.translit: Da, tam zarplata vyshe, chem u nas.

lines.english: But it's more expensive and noisier there!

lessons.tip: Compare places with чем or по сравнению с: Здесь шумнее, чем в центре. Здесь тише по сравнению с центром.

lessons.title: It doesn't work

sentences.target: Мой телефон не работает, он не включается.
sentences.english: My phone doesn't work, it won't turn on.
sentences.translit: Moy telefon ne rabotayet, on ne vklyuchayetsya.

sentences.target: Вчера сломался компьютер, и я не мог работать.
sentences.english: My computer broke yesterday and I couldn't work.
sentences.translit: Vchera slomalsya komp'yuter, i ya ne mog rabotat'.

sentences.target: Кран течёт уже три дня.
sentences.english: The tap has been leaking for three days.
sentences.translit: Kran techyot uzhe tri dnya.

sentences.target: Экран треснул, когда я его уронил.
sentences.english: The screen cracked when I dropped it.
sentences.translit: Ekran tresnul, kogda ya yevo uronil.

sentences.target: Здесь нет сигнала, я не могу позвонить.
sentences.english: There's no signal here, I can't call.
sentences.translit: Zdes' net signala, ya ne mogu pozvonit'.

sentences.target: Сайт зависает и не открывается.
sentences.english: The website freezes and won't open.
sentences.translit: Sayt zavisayet i ne otkryvayetsya.

fills.english: My phone broke yesterday.
The door won't open, I can't get in.
Water is leaking from the tap.
The computer freezes every five minutes.

dialogue.scene: Calling a friend who fixes computers

lines.target: Привет! У меня проблема. Компьютер не включается.
lines.english: Hi! I have a problem. My computer won't turn on.
lines.translit: Privet! U menya problema. Komp'yuter ne vklyuchayetsya.

lines.english: Did it work yesterday?
Yes, but today something broke.
Let me drop by and have a look.

replyOptions: Он течёт, потому что нет сигнала.

lessons.tip: Past tense for 'it broke': сломался (m), сломалась (f), сломалось (n). The verb agrees with the thing that broke.

lessons.title: Complaints

sentences.target: Добрый день, у меня проблема с заказом.
sentences.english: Good afternoon, I have a problem with my order.
sentences.translit: Dobryy den', u menya problema s zakazom.

sentences.target: Мой заказ не пришёл, а прошла уже неделя.
sentences.english: My order hasn't arrived and a week has already passed.
sentences.translit: Moy zakaz ne prishyol, a proshla uzhe nedelya.

sentences.target: Вы мне не ответили, это неприемлемо.
sentences.english: You didn't reply to me, that's unacceptable.
sentences.translit: Vy mne ne otvetili, eto nepriyemlemo.

sentences.target: Я недоволен качеством, я хочу пожаловаться.
sentences.english: I'm dissatisfied with the quality, I want to complain.
sentences.translit: Ya nedovolen kachestvom, ya khochu pozhalovat'sya.

sentences.target: Где администратор? Позовите менеджера, пожалуйста.
sentences.english: Where's the administrator? Please call the manager.
sentences.translit: Gde administrator? Pozovite menedzhera, pozhaluysta.

sentences.target: Меня обманули: это не та марка, которую я купил.
sentences.english: I was cheated: it's not the brand I bought.
sentences.translit: Menya obmanuli: eto ne ta marka, kotoruyu ya kupil.

fills.english: This is outrageous, I've been waiting for an hour!
I'm dissatisfied with the service and want to complain.
Please call the manager.
The order didn't arrive and you didn't answer me.

dialogue.scene: At a shop counter with a faulty order

lines.english: Good afternoon, how can I help?

lines.target: У меня проблема: заказ не пришёл.
lines.english: I have a problem: my order didn't arrive.
lines.translit: U menya problema: zakaz ne prishyol.

lines.english: When did you order it?

replyOptions: Десять дней назад, и никто не ответил.

lessons.tip: Polite but firm: Я хочу пожаловаться / Я требую + noun. State the problem first, ask for the person in charge second.

lessons.title: Refunds & repairs

sentences.target: Я хочу вернуть деньги, у меня есть квитанция.
sentences.english: I want my money back, I have the receipt.
sentences.translit: Ya khochu vernut' den'gi, u menya yest' kvitantsiya.

sentences.target: Можно обменять эту куртку на другой размер?
sentences.english: Can I exchange this jacket for another size?
sentences.translit: Mozhno obmenyat' etu kurtku na drugoy razmer?

sentences.target: У телефона гарантия на два года.
sentences.english: The phone has a two-year warranty.
sentences.translit: U telefona garantiya na dva goda.

sentences.target: Это брак, вы можете заменить его?
sentences.english: It's faulty, can you replace it?
sentences.translit: Eto brak, vy mozhete zamenit' yevo?

sentences.target: Мастер приедет завтра и починит кран.
sentences.english: The repairman will come tomorrow and fix the tap.
sentences.translit: Master priyedet zavtra i pochinit kran.

sentences.target: Ремонт стоит дорого, лучше купить новый.
sentences.english: The repair costs a lot, better to buy a new one.
sentences.translit: Remont stoit dorogo, luchshe kupit' novyy.

fills.english: I want to get my money back for the ticket.
Please show me the receipt.
The repairman will fix the computer tomorrow.
We have a one-year warranty, it's faulty.

dialogue.scene: Returning a faulty phone

lines.target: Здравствуйте, мой телефон сломался через неделю.
lines.english: Hello, my phone broke after a week.
lines.translit: Zdravstvuyte, moy telefon slomalsya cherez nedelyu.

lines.target: У вас есть квитанция и гарантия?
lines.english: Do you have the receipt and warranty?
lines.translit: U vas yest' kvitantsiya i garantiya?

lines.target: Да, вот они. Я хочу вернуть деньги.
lines.english: Yes, here they are. I want my money back.
lines.translit: Da, vot oni. Ya khochu vernut' den'gi.

lines.target: Хорошо, или мы можем его заменить.
lines.english: Okay, or we can replace it.
lines.translit: Khorosho, ili my mozhem yevo zamenit'.

lessons.tip: Outcomes take the perfective: хочу вернуть деньги, хочу заменить, можно починить? Ask for the finished result.

lessons.title: Apologising

sentences.target: Простите, это моя вина, я не заметил.
sentences.english: Sorry, it's my fault, I didn't notice.
sentences.translit: Prostite, eto moya vina, ya ne zametil.

sentences.target: Я не нарочно, я правда не хотел.
sentences.english: I didn't do it on purpose, I really didn't want to.
sentences.translit: Ya ne narochno, ya pravda ne khotel.

sentences.target: Больше не повторится, обещаю.
sentences.english: It won't happen again, I promise.
sentences.translit: Bol'she ne povtoritsya, obeshchayu.

sentences.target: Что можно сделать? Давайте решим вместе.
sentences.english: What can be done? Let's decide together.
sentences.translit: Shto mozhno sdelat'? Davayte reshim vmeste.

sentences.target: Я думаю, мы найдём выход и договоримся.
sentences.english: I think we'll find a way and come to an agreement.
sentences.translit: Ya dumayu, my naydyom vykhod i dogovorimsya.

sentences.target: В чём дело? Почему ты такой злой?
sentences.english: What's the matter? Why are you so angry?
sentences.translit: V chyom delo? Pochemu ty takoy zloy?

fills.english: It's my fault, sorry.
I didn't do it on purpose, honestly.
Let's solve this problem together.
We'll find a way out, don't worry.

dialogue.scene: You forgot to meet a friend

lines.target: Я ждал тебя час! Где ты был?
lines.english: I waited an hour for you! Where were you?
lines.translit: Ya zhdal tebya chas! Gde ty byl?

lines.target: Простите... то есть прости, я забыл.
lines.english: Sorry... I forgot.
lines.translit: Prostite... to yest' prosti, ya zabyl.

lines.target: Ну это уже не в первый раз!
lines.english: That's not the first time already!
lines.translit: Nu eto uzhe ne v pervyy raz!

replyOptions: Знаю, моя вина. Больше не повторится.
Я не нарочно, я ждал тебя час.
Это ты виноват, а я вернулся.

lessons.tip: Own it simply: Моя вина = my fault, Я виноват (m) / виновата (f) = I'm to blame. Then move to solutions: давайте решим.

lessons.title: Firm and polite

sentences.target: Не могли бы вы мне помочь?
sentences.english: Could you help me?
sentences.translit: Ne mogli by vy mne pomoch'?

sentences.target: Будьте так добры, повторите, пожалуйста.
sentences.english: Be so kind, please repeat that.
sentences.translit: Bud'te tak dobry, povtorite, pozhaluysta.

sentences.target: Послушайте, давайте спокойно поговорим.
sentences.english: Listen, let's talk calmly.
sentences.translit: Poslushayte, davayte spokoyno pogovorim.

sentences.target: Это недоразумение, вы меня не поняли.
sentences.english: It's a misunderstanding, you didn't understand me.
sentences.translit: Eto nedorazumeniye, vy menya ne ponyali.

sentences.target: Повторяю: это не моя вина, и я настаиваю на возврате.
sentences.english: I repeat: it's not my fault, and I insist on a refund.
sentences.translit: Povtoryayu: eto ne moya vina, i ya nastaivayu na vozvrate.

sentences.target: Я подам жалобу, если вы не ответите.
sentences.english: I'll file a complaint if you don't reply.
sentences.translit: Ya podam zhalobu, yesli vy ne otvetite.

fills.english: Could you wait a minute?
Be so kind as to open the window.
It's a misunderstanding, you didn't understand me.
I insist, this is the last time.

dialogue.scene: A heated moment at a hotel desk

lines.target: Мы не можем вернуть вам деньги.
lines.english: We can't give you your money back.
lines.translit: My ne mozhem vernut' vam den'gi.

lines.english: Listen, let's stay calm.

lines.target: Я спокоен, но это не наша вина.
lines.english: I'm calm, but it's not our fault.
lines.translit: Ya spokoyen, no eto ne nasha vina.

replyOptions: Не могли бы вы позвать менеджера?
Как вам не стыдно, я настаиваю вчера.

lessons.tip: Не могли бы вы + infinitive = would you mind...? A soft way to sound firm. Add будьте так добры for extra politeness.

lessons.title: I prefer

items.english: I don't mind / it's all the same

sentences.target: Я предпочитаю чай, а не кофе.
sentences.english: I prefer tea, not coffee.
sentences.translit: Ya predpochitayu chay, a ne kofe.

sentences.target: Мне больше нравится жить в городе.
sentences.english: I like living in the city more.
sentences.translit: Mne bol'she nravitsya zhit' v gorode.

sentences.target: Лучше всего я сплю в субботу.
sentences.english: I sleep best on Saturday.
sentences.translit: Luchshe vsevo ya splyu v subbotu.

sentences.target: Давай возьмём такси вместо автобуса.
sentences.english: Let's take a taxi instead of the bus.
sentences.translit: Davay voz'myom taksi vmesto avtobusa.

sentences.target: Это хороший вариант, но на мой вкус слишком дорогой.
sentences.english: It's a good option, but too expensive to my taste.
sentences.translit: Eto khoroshiy variant, no na moy vkus slishkom dorogoy.

sentences.target: Куда пойдём? Мне всё равно, выбирай ты.
sentences.english: Where shall we go? I don't mind, you choose.
sentences.translit: Kuda poydyom? Mne vsyo ravno, vybiray ty.

fills.english: I prefer tea, not coffee.
Take water instead of beer.
What do you want? I don't mind, you choose.
That's a very good option, I agree.

dialogue.scene: Deciding on a place to eat

lines.english: Do you want pizza or sushi?

lines.target: Хм, я бы предпочёл суши. А ты?
lines.english: Hm, I'd prefer sushi. And you?
lines.translit: Khm, ya by predpochyol sushi. A ty?

lines.english: I don't mind, you choose.

replyOptions: Тогда суши, лучше всего там рыба.

lessons.tip: Я предпочитаю + accusative: Я предпочитаю чай (not кофе). For 'rather than' use вместо + genitive: вместо кофе.

lessons.title: Который & co

sentences.target: Это человек, который работает со мной.
sentences.english: This is the person who works with me.
sentences.translit: Eto chelovek, kotoryy rabotayet so mnoy.

sentences.target: Книга, которую я читаю, очень интересная.
sentences.english: The book I'm reading is very interesting.
sentences.translit: Kniga, kotoruyu ya chitayu, ochen' interesnaya.

sentences.target: Это место, где я люблю отдыхать.
sentences.english: This is the place where I like to relax.
sentences.translit: Eto mesto, gde ya lyublyu otdykhat'.

sentences.target: Я не понимаю то, что ты говоришь.
sentences.english: I don't understand what you're saying.
sentences.translit: Ya ne ponimayu to, shto ty govorish'.

sentences.target: Кто-то звонил, но я не знаю кто.
sentences.english: Someone called, but I don't know who.
sentences.translit: Kto-to zvonil, no ya ne znayu kto.

sentences.target: Когда-нибудь я поеду в Россию.
sentences.english: Someday I'll go to Russia.
sentences.translit: Kogda-nibud' ya poyedu v Rossiyu.

fills.english: I like the girl who works here.
The film we watched was boring.
I want something sweet and cold.
That's the man who lives nearby.

dialogue.scene: Describing a café you found

lines.english: Where were you last night?

lines.target: Я нашёл место, где делают отличный кофе.
lines.english: I found a place where they make great coffee.
lines.translit: Ya nashyol mesto, gde delayut otlichnyy kofe.

lines.english: Really? Where is it?

replyOptions: Где-то около метро, я покажу тебе.

lessons.tip: который agrees in gender and number with the noun it follows, and takes the case of its own role: книга, которую я читаю (feminine, accusative).

lessons.title: Taste

sentences.target: Я люблю острую еду, а он любит сладкое.
sentences.english: I like spicy food, and he likes sweets.
sentences.translit: Ya lyublyu ostruyu yedu, a on lyubit sladkoye.

sentences.target: Суп слишком солёный, а кофе горький.
sentences.english: The soup is too salty and the coffee bitter.
sentences.translit: Sup slishkom solyonyy, a kofe gor'kiy.

sentences.target: Мама готовит вкусные домашние котлеты.
sentences.english: Mum makes tasty homemade burgers.
sentences.translit: Mama gotovit vkusnyye domashniye kotlety.

sentences.target: Я заказал жареную рыбу и варёную картошку.
sentences.english: I ordered fried fish and boiled potatoes.
sentences.translit: Ya zakazal zharenuyu rybu i varyonuyu kartoshku.

sentences.target: У меня нет аппетита, я на диете.
sentences.english: I have no appetite, I'm on a diet.
sentences.translit: U menya net appetita, ya na diyete.

sentences.target: Это яблоко кислое, но мне нравится этот вкус.
sentences.english: This apple is sour, but I like the taste.
sentences.translit: Eto yabloko kisloye, no mne nravitsya etot vkus.

fills.english: This soup is very spicy, I can't eat it.
I like baked potato.
The tea is sweet, I don't like it like that.
I have no appetite, I feel unwell.

dialogue.scene: Tasting a dish at a friend's house

lines.english: Try it, it's homemade soup!
Tasty, but it's a bit spicy.
Shall I add bread or water?

lessons.tip: Taste adjectives are regular: острый суп (m), острая еда (f), острое мясо (n), острые блюда (pl).

lessons.title: Lifestyle

sentences.target: Мой образ жизни очень простой: работа, дом, сон.
sentences.english: My lifestyle is very simple: work, home, sleep.
sentences.translit: Moy obraz zhizni ochen' prostoy: rabota, dom, son.

sentences.target: У меня есть одна плохая привычка.
sentences.english: I have one bad habit.
sentences.translit: U menya yest' odna plokhaya privychka.

sentences.target: Я интересуюсь музыкой и занимаюсь спортом.
sentences.english: I'm interested in music and I do sport.
sentences.translit: Ya interesuyus' muzykoy i zanimayus' sportom.

sentences.target: В свободное время мой досуг — это фильмы.
sentences.english: In my free time my leisure is films.
sentences.translit: V svobodnoye vremya moy dosug — eto fil'my.

sentences.target: Какое у тебя хобби? Какие у тебя увлечения?
sentences.english: What's your hobby? What are your interests?
sentences.translit: Kakoye u tebya khobbi? Kakiye u tebya uvlecheniya?

sentences.target: По-моему, у нас разные вкусы и разные мнения.
sentences.english: I think we have different tastes and different opinions.
sentences.translit: Po-moyemu, u nas raznyye vkusy i raznyye mneniya.

fills.english: I'm interested in music, and my brother in football.
I do sport every morning.
I have a simple routine, I get up at seven.
I have a new hobby, I really like it.

dialogue.scene: Getting to know a new colleague

lines.target: А чем ты интересуешься вне работы?
lines.english: And what are you interested in outside work?
lines.translit: A chem ty interesuyesh'sya vne raboty?

lines.target: Я занимаюсь спортом и люблю кино.
lines.english: I do sport and I like films.
lines.translit: Ya zanimayus' sportom i lyublyu kino.

lines.english: Great! What's your routine like?

replyOptions: Я встаю рано и бегаю каждое утро.
Я интересуюсь режимом, потому что хобби.

lessons.tip: Interests use the instrumental: интересуюсь музыкой, занимаюсь спортом. No preposition needed.

lessons.title: Recommendations

sentences.target: Стоит ли ехать в Москву зимой?
sentences.english: Is it worth going to Moscow in winter?
sentences.translit: Stoit li yekhat' v Moskvu zimoy?

sentences.target: Что лучше: поезд или самолёт?
sentences.english: Which is better: train or plane?
sentences.translit: Shto luchshe: poyezd ili samolyot?

sentences.target: Что посоветуете на ужин?
sentences.english: What would you recommend for dinner?
sentences.translit: Shto posovetuyete na uzhin?

sentences.target: Я рекомендую этот ресторан, там очень вкусно.
sentences.english: I recommend this restaurant, it's really tasty.
sentences.translit: Ya rekomenduyu etot restoran, tam ochen' vkusno.

sentences.target: Не советую брать эту куртку, она слишком дорогая.
sentences.english: I don't advise getting that jacket, it's too expensive.
sentences.translit: Ne sovetuyu brat' etu kurtku, ona slishkom dorogaya.

sentences.target: Как вы думаете, в чём разница между ними?
sentences.english: What do you think the difference between them is?
sentences.translit: Kak vy dumayete, v chyom raznitsa mezhdu nimi?

fills.english: Is it worth going to this museum?
What would you recommend for breakfast?
I recommend this soup.
What's the difference between these phones?

dialogue.scene: Asking a waiter for advice

lines.english: Hello! What will you order?
What would you recommend?

lines.target: Рекомендую жареную рыбу, она у нас самая популярная.
lines.english: I recommend the fried fish, it's our most popular.
lines.translit: Rekomenduyu zharenuyu rybu, ona u nas samaya populyarnaya.

replyOptions: Хорошо, возьму её. Что лучше к ней?

lessons.tip: Что посоветуете? = What would you recommend? Ask Стоит ли ...? (is it worth ...?) with an infinitive.

lessons.title: I would like

items.english: I'd like to / I'd feel like

sentences.target: Я бы хотел чашку чая с лимоном.
sentences.english: I'd like a cup of tea with lemon.
sentences.translit: Ya by khotel chashku chaya s limonom.

sentences.target: Я бы выпил что-нибудь холодное.
sentences.english: I'd drink something cold.
sentences.translit: Ya by vypil shto-nibud' kholodnoye.

sentences.target: Мне бы хотелось поехать к морю.
sentences.english: I'd like to go to the sea.
sentences.translit: Mne by khotelos' poyekhat' k moryu.

sentences.target: Я бы не отказался от пиццы.
sentences.english: I wouldn't say no to pizza.
sentences.translit: Ya by ne otkazalsya ot pitstsy.

sentences.target: Было бы здорово встретиться на выходных!
sentences.english: It would be great to meet at the weekend!
sentences.translit: Bylo by zdorovo vstretit'sya na vykhodnykh!

sentences.target: Лучше бы мы остались дома.
sentences.english: We'd better have stayed at home.
sentences.translit: Luchshe by my ostalis' doma.

fills.english: I'd like coffee with milk.
I'd eat something spicy.
It would be great to go to the sea in summer.
I'd like to rest a little.

dialogue.scene: Deciding what to do on a Saturday

lines.english: What shall we do on Saturday?

lines.target: Я бы пошёл в парк, а ты?
lines.english: I'd go to the park, what about you?
lines.translit: Ya by poshyol v park, a ty?

lines.english: I'd rather stay at home.

replyOptions: Тогда давай останемся, я не против.
Тогда я бы пошёл вчера в парк.
Я не отказался дома, потому что.

lessons.tip: бы + past tense = would: я бы выпил кофе (I'd have a coffee). Women say я бы хотела, я бы выпила. The verb still shows gender, never future.

lessons.title: Hypotheticals

sentences.target: Если бы я был богатым, я бы купил дом.
sentences.english: If I were rich, I'd buy a house.
sentences.translit: Yesli by ya byl bogatym, ya by kupil dom.

sentences.target: Если бы у меня было время, я бы поехал с вами.
sentences.english: If I had time, I'd go with you.
sentences.translit: Yesli by u menya bylo vremya, ya by poyekhal s vami.

sentences.target: Если бы я знал, я бы тебе сказал.
sentences.english: If I'd known, I'd have told you.
sentences.translit: Yesli by ya znal, ya by tebe skazal.

sentences.target: Если бы не дождь, мы бы пошли гулять.
sentences.english: If it weren't for the rain, we'd go for a walk.
sentences.translit: Yesli by ne dozhd', my by poshli gulyat'.

sentences.target: А вдруг он не придёт? Что тогда?
sentences.english: What if he doesn't come? What then?
sentences.translit: A vdrug on ne pridyot? Shto togda?

sentences.target: На твоём месте я бы позвонил ему.
sentences.english: In your place I'd call him.
sentences.translit: Na tvoyom meste ya by pozvonil yemu.

fills.after: я мог, я бы помог тебе.
fills.english: If I could, I'd help you.
If I had time, I'd come.
In your place I'd stay at home.
Let's say we go to the cinema. What next?

dialogue.scene: Daydreaming with a friend

lines.target: Представь, что у тебя много денег.
lines.english: Imagine you have lots of money.
lines.translit: Predstav', shto u tebya mnogo deneg.

lines.target: Если бы я был богатым, я бы бросил работу.
lines.english: If I were rich, I'd quit my job.
lines.translit: Yesli by ya byl bogatym, ya by brosil rabotu.

lines.english: And what would you do?

replyOptions: Если бы я делал, потому что.

lessons.tip: Если бы + past, то бы + past: Если бы я знал, я бы сказал. Both halves use the past form with бы, even for the present or future.

lessons.title: Dreams

items.english: to buy a house by the sea
to make a dream come true

sentences.target: Я мечтаю о доме у моря.
sentences.english: I dream of a house by the sea.
sentences.translit: Ya mechtayu o dome u morya.

sentences.target: Если бы я был богатым, я бы объехал мир.
sentences.english: If I were rich, I'd travel around the world.
sentences.translit: Yesli by ya byl bogatym, ya by obyekhal mir.

sentences.target: Он мечтает стать знаменитым.
sentences.english: He dreams of becoming famous.
sentences.translit: On mechtayet stat' znamenitym.

sentences.target: Я хочу бросить работу и начать с нуля.
sentences.english: I want to quit my job and start from scratch.
sentences.translit: Ya khochu brosit' rabotu i nachat' s nulya.

sentences.translit: Sestra khochet zhit' za granitsey i stat' vrachom.

fills.english: I dream of a house by the sea.
If I won the lottery, I'd buy a house.
Some day I'll make my dream come true.
I want to quit my job and go to Russia.

dialogue.scene: Late-night talk about the future

lines.english: What do you dream about?

lines.target: Я мечтаю жить за границей и свободно говорить по-русски.
lines.english: I dream of living abroad and speaking Russian fluently.
lines.translit: Ya mechtayu zhit' za granitsey i svobodno govorit' po-russki.

lines.english: Great! And when will you start?

replyOptions: Я уже начал, я учу русский каждый день.
Я мечтаю о лотерею, потому что.

lessons.tip: мечтать о + prepositional: мечтаю о доме, мечтаю о море. Stack infinitives after хочу or мечтаю: мечтаю жить за границей.

lessons.title: Advice

sentences.target: Тебе стоит больше спать.
sentences.english: You should sleep more.
sentences.translit: Tebe stoit bol'she spat'.

sentences.target: Тебе следует позвонить маме.
sentences.english: You ought to call your mum.
sentences.translit: Tebe sleduyet pozvonit' mame.

sentences.target: Я бы посоветовал тебе не торопиться.

sentences.translit: Ya by posovetoval tebe ne toropit'sya.

sentences.target: Попробуй этот суп, он очень вкусный.
sentences.english: Try this soup, it's very tasty.
sentences.translit: Poprobuy etot sup, on ochen' vkusnyy.

sentences.target: Не стоит так нервничать, всё будет хорошо.

sentences.translit: Ne stoit tak nervnichat', vsyo budet khorosho.

sentences.target: Держи меня в курсе и имей в виду: я всегда рядом.

sentences.translit: Derzhi menya v kurse i imey v vidu: ya vsegda ryadom.

fills.english: You should rest, you're very tired.
Don't rush, we have plenty of time.
I'd advise you to call him.
Think again before deciding.

dialogue.scene: Listening to a stressed friend

lines.target: Я так устал, у меня нет сил.
lines.english: I'm so tired, I have no strength.
lines.translit: Ya tak ustal, u menya net sil.

lines.english: You should rest.
But I have so much work!

replyOptions: Не стоит так нервничать, работа подождёт.

lessons.tip: Тебе стоит / следует + infinitive = you should. Formal 'you' is вам: Вам стоит отдохнуть. Soft imperatives: попробуй, подумай, отдохни.

lessons.tip: Пусть + he/she/they = let them / may they: пусть он придёт. Wish for something: хочу, чтобы + past tense: хочу, чтобы ты приехал.
